summary: Escalating geopolitical conflict in the Middle East and volatile crude prices are severely straining global shipping lanes and inflating maritime freight rates, forcing major Asian economies like India and China to rely on energy sanction waivers to maintain fuel security. In response to a widening trade deficit that crossed $100 billion with China, India is pairing aggressive central bank currency-defense measures with targeted port and highway infrastructure investments to stabilize its macro environment. Looking ahead, ongoing Red Sea security threats will keep maritime freight surcharges elevated and drive shippers toward alternative corridors, while forcing Beijing and New Delhi into deeper diplomatic negotiations to mitigate non-tariff trade barriers.
